sentences.text: 1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 23.09.2019 passed in MVC No.224/2019 by the Court of Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-IV at Davangere (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. On 10.01.2019 the deceased Halesh Prabhudev Patil while travelling in a car bearing Registration Prabhudev Patil S vs Pavankumar K S on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187279361/
2 No.KA-31/M- 9176 met with an accident as the driver of the car/respondent No.1 drove the car in a rash and negligent manner near Tumbrigod Village and succumbed to the injuries.
Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are his parents and petitioner No.3 is his brother.
4. The deceased was a BE (Civil Engineering) student.

The tribunal has considered his notional income at Rs.18,000/- per month and has awarded a sum of Rs.19,74,000/- as compensation payable with 8% per annum interest from the date of petition till realization.
Not satisfied with the same, the present appeal is filed by the petitioners therein.
The Insurance Company has accepted the liability and has not preferred any appeal.
5. The only question that arises for consideration is whether the compensation awarded is just and fair.
6. The tribunal based on the evidence let in has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.18,000/- per month, the same is not disputed by the insurance company.
The deceased at the time of accident was aged 19 years and a multiplier of '18' has to be adopted
as per the decision laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121].

sentences.text: As he was a bachelor, 50% is deducted towards his personal expenses and towards future prospects 40% is added to his income, as per the law down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680.

sentences.text: Thus towards loss of dependency the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.18,000 x 12 x 18 + 40%/2 = Rs.27,21,600/-.

Towards loss of estate and funeral expenses a sum of Rs.30,000/- is hereby awarded and towards loss of consortium the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each and together have entitled a sum of Rs.1,20,000/-.

Thus in all petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.28,71,600/- under the following heads:
SL.NO. HEADS OF COMPENSATION COMPENSATION COMPENSATION AWARDED AWARDED BY BEFORE THIS COURT TRIBUNAL (AMT (AMT IN RS.)
IN RS.) 1 Loss of 19,44,000 27,21,600 Dependency 2 Loss of estate 15,000 15,000 3 Funeral expenses 15,000 15,000 4 Loss of - 1,20,000 consortium
Thus the petitioners are entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.8,97,600/- over and above what has been awarded by the tribunal.
Taking the bank rate of interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition before the tribunal till realization on the enhanced amount.

Hence, the following order:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Petitioners are entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.8,97,600/- along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition before the tribunal till realization which shall be over and above what has been awarded by the tribunal.
